Indian Standard 
BONDED ABRASIVE GRINDING WHEELS 





PART 


1 


PROFILES AND TYPES 




( Second Revision ) 


1. Scope — Covers the basic profiles and types of bonded abrasive grinding wheels. This standard 
does not include the mounted points since these have already been covered in IS : 3300-1980 
' Dimensions for mounted points \

4. Shape and Types of Grinding Wheels — Basically all abrasive wheels utilize either the 
periphery ( T ) or the wall ( W ) as the grinding surface. 

4.1 Plain wheel is the simplest form of peripheral grinding wheel, ( see Type 1 ) and straight cup 
wheel is the simplest form of wall grinding wheel ( see Type 6 ). 

Type 1 Straight wheel : Peripheral grinding wheel having a diameter, thickness and hole.

Type 2 Cylinder wheel : Side grinding wheel having a diameter, thickness and wall, 
mounted on the diameter, or a similar wheel mounted in a chuck or on a plate.

TYPE 2 



Type 5 Wheel, recessed one side : Peripheral grinding wheel having one side straight or flat 
and the opposite side recessed. A recessed wheel allows a wider faced grinding wheel to be used 
when the available mounting thickness ( £ ) is less than the required overall thickness ( T ) . The 
recess allows grinding clearance for the nut and flange. 



■00 
-OP- 



F l

|^— «>H— • 



TYPE 5 



Type 6 Straight cup wheel : Side grinding wheel having a diameter, thickness and hole with 
one side straight or flat and opposite side recessed. This type, however, differs from Type 5 in 
that the grinding is performed by the wall (W). The wall dimension {W) takes precedence 
over the diameter of recess as an essential inter-mediate dimension to describe this shape type.

IS 2324: (Parti)- 1985 

Type 7 Wheel, recessed two sides -.Peripheral grinding wheel having both sides recessed to 
allow grinding clearance for both flanges or recessed so that an unusually wide faced wheel may 
be mounted when the available mounting thickness ( £ ) is less than the overall thickness ( T ) . 




Type 11 Flaring-cup wheel : Side grinding wheel having a wall flared or tapered outward from 
the back. Wall thickness at the back is normally greater than at the grinding face ( W ) . 





TYPE 11 

Type 12 Dish wheel : Side grinding wheel known as a dish, differing from a Type 11 in that 
Type 12 always has a ( U ) dimension. The W dimension of a Type 11 becomes the ( A ) dimension 
of a Type 12. The grinding may be performed by the ( U ) face. 




TYPE 12 

Type 13 Saucer wheel : Peripheral grinding wheel known as a saucer, differing from a Type 12 
in that the cross section is equal throughout ( U — £) . 

The face is always half-round with R « x-. 




Note— Arrows indicate grinding surface. 



IS : 2324 (Parti )- 1985 

4.2 On all cones and plugs grinding is performed by all surfaces except the flat ( dimension 
'D' ) on the mounting side. These shape normally have a blind hole threaded bushing for mounting. 

Type 16 Cone curved side ; Curved sided cone with a radius nose sometimes referred to as 
'Bullet Shape'. 




TYPE 16 

Type 17 and 17R : Cone with straight side, square tip and round tip.

Type 19 and 19R ; Plug — Conical end, square Tip and Round tip — Combination cone and plug 
with a square tip similar to Type 17 and the cylindrical portions similar to Type 18. The cylindrical 
portion ( S ) is normally equal to or greater than the depth of the blind hole threaded bushing (fl).

4.3 A relieved side is a depression in the side of a wheel which is tapered from a radial flat at the 
periphery ( A ) to an inside flat ( K ) or recess diameter ( P ) . 

Type 20 Wheel, relieved one side : Peripheral grinding wheel having one side straight or flat 
and the other side relieved to a flat.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

The standard, 'Dimensions for grinding wheels (other than internal grinding wheels)' 
IS : 2324, was first published in 1963 and subsequently first revision was done in 1971. The current 
revision has been taken up to bring it in line with the work done at ISO level as well as for includ- 
ing the profiles and types of the bonded abrasive grinding wheels. Further this revised standard 
has been printed in two parts: 

IS : 2324 ( Part 1 )-1985 Bonded abrasive grinding wheels: Part 1 Profiles and types 

IS : 2324 ( Part 2 )-1985 Bonded abrasive grinding wheel: Part 2 Dimensions 

This standard deals with the profiles and types of bonded abrasive grinding wheels which are 
most commonly used. The dimension and tolerances of the? a abrasive grinding wheels are covered 
in IS : 2324 ( Part 2 ) -1985. Typa 27 A and Typa 28 grinding wheels have not been covered, since 
these are not being used in the country. 

While preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from ANSI B 74: 2-1982 'Specifi- 
cation for shapes and sizes of grinding wheels and for shapes, sizes and identification of mounted 
wheels' issued by American National Standards Institute. 



Prlntfd at Mew India Printing Presa, Khurja, India
